newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Chinese restraint on islands row wins Lee's praise.
newsitem.headline: Chinese restraint on islands row wins Lee's praise.

text.p: Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew praised China for showing restraint in a dispute over islands in the East China Sea, the Straits Times newspaper said on Thursday.
The newspaper said Lee noted in an interview that activists from Hong Kong and Taiwan, but not China, had been landing on the disputed islands, called the Diaoyus by China and the Senkakus by Japan.
"That shows a certain restraint. They could easily have made it a big deal," Lee was quoted as saying.
"China has been very cool, firm, but no histrionics. That sums up their policy for the next 10 to 20 years."
Japan has claimed the islands since 1895 while Chinese claims are centuries-old.
The dispute flared anew in July when Japanese right-wingers erected a crude lighthouse on one of the islands to underscore Tokyo's claim.
Hong Kong and Taiwan activists culiminated weeks of subsequent anti-Japanese protests with a joint landing on the islands on Monday.
An earlier landing attempt resulted in the drowning of a Hong Kong activist.
